_note: Catalog for the all-courses gallery (pages/courses.html). One entry per course shown in the gallery. `deck` resolves that deck's cover_image_url from tarot/_collection.json at render time (so thumbnails follow the deck art); `thumb` is a direct image path when a deck cover isn't the right image. Keep the id/title in step with COURSE_GROUPS in site-header.js (the dropdown menu) — this file is the gallery's data, that array is the menu's. An entry may carry `href` (a page other than a course, e.g. a spread in the Caster) and `go` (its link label). Research chapters open in the course viewer as id "../research/<file>".

courses.title: The History of Tarot
courses.blurb: Six centuries, from a 1440s card game, through the occult reinvention of 1781, to today — read closely, deck by deck.

courses.title: How the Cards Can Work
courses.blurb: A reading doesn't tell your fate — it might help you make it. The honest case, with the evidence.

courses.title: Ways to Contribute
courses.blurb: Everything here is open data (CC BY-SA) in one open repo. Fix or add a deck, a spread, a course — by the gentlest route that suits you.

courses.title: Reading the Cards
courses.blurb: The full anthology — why read at all, setting the intention, and the ecosystem of voices to read through.

courses.title: Intention Setting
courses.blurb: Why still read tarot after it disappointed you — not as a fate, but as a gate — and the lenses to read through.

courses.title: The Order of the Trumps
courses.blurb: Who set the order of the twenty-two trumps, and what it meant: three Italian orders, a preacher's list, the 1781 reversal, and why the Golden Dawn moved Strength and Justice.

courses.title: Same Card, Every Deck
courses.blurb: (Draft) Five centuries of the same twenty-two pictures in one comparable grid — a hands-on course in telling correlation from copying, and copying from a shared ancestor. Two sections live; six more on the way.

courses.title: Your Card Table
courses.blurb: (Draft) Areas of your life down the side, less · keep · more across the top, one card in each cell. Then sit with it and decide. A practice, a notation, and a table to try.

courses.title: The Ontoject, One Life
courses.blurb: (Study) The trumps of the Ontoject deck read as one life, from before conception to return, with the poem the deck grew from, an animated page, and why the Fool was never the Joker.

courses.title: Tarot as a Source of Fiction
courses.blurb: A publisher asked Calvino for a few pages about a fifteenth-century deck; he came back with a novel built out of the cards, then confessed exactly where he cheated. The writer, the commission, the machine — and how to run it yourself.

courses.title: Tarot & the Crack
courses.blurb: From wanting one perfect system to explain the cosmos, to living with the crack that is always there. Why PlayfulProcess still shuffles the cards.

courses.title: The Golden Dawn — the Map and the Walk
courses.blurb: The most influential reading system the cards ever wore — Book T, the decans, the Rider-Waite-Smith deck that grew from it — and the pathworking practice that goes with it: each trump a gate you choose to walk through. Not prophecy.

courses.title: Where the Cards Went
courses.blurb: The Order wrote its tarot down but never printed a deck. From hand-copied cards to Wang, Dowson, the Ciceros and Thoth.

courses.title: Dignities, not Reversals
courses.blurb: Book T reads a card by its neighbours and has no rule for a card upside down.

courses.title: The Golden Dawn: the Research Chapter
courses.blurb: The founding and its forged pedigree, Book T, the schism of 1900, and who was in it.

courses.title: Crowley & Harris: the Thoth Tarot
courses.blurb: Why the name Thoth, what Crowley said he was doing, and what changed from Book T.

courses.title: How Could Kant Read the Tarot?
courses.blurb: Kant and tarot-as-divination were exact contemporaries. A reading from reason and duty.

courses.title: How Could DBT Read the Tarot?
courses.blurb: Dialectical Behavior Therapy at the card table: accept what is, and change it.

courses.title: Jung Reads the Tarot
courses.blurb: Not your future but your unlived life: the shadow, the archetype, the figure waiting to be made conscious.

courses.title: The Non-Dual Tantra Lens
courses.blurb: The card as play of consciousness greeting itself; a hard card is a move in a game you co-author.

courses.title: The Post-Activism Lens
courses.blurb: The card as a sanctuary where the stuck and the unspeakable can be hosted, not fixed.

courses.title: The Hospicing-Modernity Lens
courses.blurb: Staying with what is dying and what is being born, without rushing to hope.

courses.title: Morality Is an Ecosystem
courses.blurb: Why no single voice owns the meaning of a card: morality grows between many, like an ecosystem.

courses.title: Why a Reading Feels So Personal
courses.blurb: The chill is real; its explanation is documented psychology, not hidden knowledge. A deep dive into the evidence.

courses.title: What a Reading Can Do
courses.blurb: Four non-magical mechanisms with real evidence — projection, re-narration, productive randomness, ritual — and the stance that unlocks them.

courses.title: Tarot Today
courses.blurb: A living question: why a card game is having a cultural moment, read against the data.

courses.title: How Humans Have Cast Lots
courses.blurb: Yarrow stalks, oracle bones, the Pythia, rune-staves: structured randomness long before tarot.

courses.title: Games of the Tarot
courses.blurb: A player's companion to the card game tarot was for its first three centuries.

courses.title: Spread: Test the Spirits
courses.blurb: Seven cards to test a voice by where it leads and what it grows. After Ignatius, Matthew 7 and the Kalama Sutta.

courses.title: Working with Claude Desktop
courses.blurb: The powerful path for contributors: GitHub and git from zero, the session habits that keep work safe, and a private-folder pattern.
